title: Seedless Raspberry Sorbet
changes_from_base: Sieved raspberries in a light syrup with corn syrup replace the mango and lime; part of the base is frozen first so it churns quickly.
summary: A vivid, smooth raspberry sorbet: the purée is sieved free of seeds and part of the base is frozen ahead so it churns extra smooth.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Warm the water, sugar and salt in the small pan just until the sugar dissolves, then cool for 10 min.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the raspberries, the warm syrup, corn syrup and lemon juice for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Sieve
steps.text: Press it through the sieve with the back of a ladle, scraping the underside, until only dry seeds are left.

steps.title: Split and chill
steps.text: Pour 250 ml into a small bowl and freeze it; refrigerate the rest. Leave both for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Scrape the frozen portion into the cold base and stir until it melts; this makes the mix extra cold so it churns faster and smoother.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn for 15-25 min, until thick and paler, pack firmly into the container and freeze for at least 2 h.

tips: Frozen raspberries are just as good as fresh here; thaw them first.
Scrape the underside of the sieve; a lot of the thick purée clings there.
Serve with a little whipped cream or a crisp biscuit.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer for up to 5 days. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
